name: Synthetic mortality table and survival engine
description: The deterministic heart of the demo. A generated, clearly synthetic mortality table for ages 0 to 120 (male and female), and a pure survival engine that turns it into survivor counts. Everything visual is built on this, so it comes first and ships with the full test set from fade/standards/testing.md.

userStories.title: Generate the synthetic mortality table
userStories.description: tools/generate-table.mjs writes data/mortality.csv with columns age,qx_male,qx_female for ages 0 to 120 using a Gompertz-Makeham curve with fixed constants (no randomness). Female rates are lower than male at every age above 0. q(120) is exactly 1 for both.
acceptanceCriteria: node tools/generate-table.mjs writes data/mortality.csv with a header and exactly 121 data rows
Running the generator twice produces byte-identical files
q(0) is between 0.002 and 0.006 (infant mortality bump), q(x) is monotone non-decreasing from age 10 onwards, q(120) = 1
The CSV begins with a comment line: '# SYNTHETIC illustrative mortality. Not for real actuarial use.' and the loader skips comment lines
The constants and the formula are documented in a module comment

userStories.title: Table loader with validation
userStories.description: src/engine/table.mjs exports parseTable(csvText) returning { male: number[121], female: number[121] } and throws a clear error if any age is missing, duplicated, or any rate is outside [0, 1].
acceptanceCriteria: parseTable on data/mortality.csv returns two arrays of length 121 indexed by age
A table missing an age, or with a rate of 1.2, throws an Error whose message names the age
tests/table.test.mjs covers the happy path and both failure cases and passes under node --test

userStories.title: Survival engine
userStories.description: src/engine/survival.mjs exports survivors(cohort, qx, startAge) returning an array of fractional survivor counts indexed by age from startAge to 121 (the entry for 121 is 0), and applyImprovement(qx, pct) returning a new array with every rate scaled by (1 - pct). Pure functions, no rounding.
acceptanceCriteria: survivors(1000000, qx, 0)[0] === 1000000 and the last entry is 0
Counts never increase with age; zero mortality gives no deaths; q = 1 at age a gives 0 from a + 1 on
applyImprovement(qx, 0.1) at every age equals 0.9 * qx within 1e-12, and improved survivors are >= baseline at every age
applyImprovement rejects pct outside [0, 0.3] with an Error
tests/survival.test.mjs implements items 2 to 7 of fade/standards/testing.md and passes

userStories.title: Independent reference check
userStories.description: tools/reference.py is a standalone Python script that reads data/mortality.csv and prints survivors from a cohort of 1,000,000 at starting age 0 for ages 30, 65, 90 and 110, male and female, and writes them to data/reference.json. It is written from the formula alone, without importing or reading the JS engine. A test compares the JS engine to the JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: python3 tools/reference.py writes data/reference.json with the eight values
tests/reference.test.mjs reads data/reference.json and asserts the JS engine matches each value to within 0.5
The test passes. If it does not, fix the engine, not the reference, and record the discrepancy in fade/progress.md

technicalNotes.rationale: Small, well-specified numerical code. The tests are the deliverable.
